sasha: Heads up — after deploying continuous-batching tweak v2 (batch fusion + queue-policy update) at 03:45 UTC, we're seeing a 30-60ms 95th latency jump on short-token requests (~<=32 tokens). https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/serving/runtime-latency

lucas: saw the spike too, looks focused on low-seq paths. P95 on small requests up ~45ms for the last 30m.

maya: any correlating throughput drop?

sasha: throughput mostly steady, CPU GPU util normal. but per-kernel tail latency looks weird.

devin: can you paste the kernel-selector logs from the affected host?

sasha: pasted below (host g1-42):
```
[2026-03-16T03:46:01Z] batch_id=9043 shape=(8,16) selector=fast_gemm_v2 chosen_kernel=gemm_tile_128x64
[2026-03-16T03:46:01Z] batch_id=9044 shape=(3,8) selector=fast_gemm_v2 chosen_kernel=gemm_generic
[2026-03-16T03:46:02Z] batch_id=9045 shape=(2,6) selector=fast_gemm_v2 chosen_kernel=gemm_generic
[2026-03-16T03:46:02Z] batch_id=9046 shape=(12,32) selector=fast_gemm_v2 chosen_kernel=gemm_tile_256x128
```

lucas: note: selector=fast_gemm_v2 is our new heuristic that picks based on fused batch shape, not per-request seq distribution. Looks like small batches are getting generic kernels.

maya: perf-bot profile for that 10:03 window (affected host):
```
perf-bot: time spent per function: select_kernel_for_batch 31%, cudnn_gemm_generic 52%, kv_cache_lookup 6%, packing/unpack 7%, other 4%
```

devin: cudnn_gemm_generic at 52% on GPU is bad — that's our slow path for irregular shapes. Why did selector pick generic for the small fused batches?

sasha: hypothesis: batch fusion is coalescing small, dissimilar seqs into an odd shape (e.g., batch_size 3 with padded seqs) that confuses the selector's tile-fit scoring. The selector currently only looks at (batch_size, seq_len_max) and a simple shape-compat map.

lucas: can we repro locally by forcing that fusion behavior? I can try a stress test to create many small heterogeneous requests.

maya: also seeing increased contention on KV cache (small reqs hit KV hot keys more). KV lock wait up ~15% in same window. Could amplify latency.

devin: quick fix idea: revert the selector to consult historical kernel p95 for a shape bin before picking generic path. Or temporarily disable batch fusion for sequences<32.

sasha: rollback of batch-fusion-for-short-reqs sounds safe. If we A/B it, we can confirm.

lucas: running a canary rollout now: disabling fusion for seq<=32 on g1 pool. command: `infractl rollout set continuous-batching.fusion.max_seq=31 --pool g1 --canary 10%`

perf-bot: canary started at 03:59 UTC on pool g1 (10% traffic).

maya: initial 5m after canary looks promising — p95 for small requests down ~28ms on canary instances.

devin: still need long-term: update selector scoring to consider tile-efficiency and fallback cost. I'll sketch a patch: 1) compute estimated_ops_per_token for candidate kernel, 2) include measured historical_latency_bin for shape, 3) prefer kernels with stable p95.

sasha: also adjust queue-policy token budget: our current token_budget target (tb=256) allowed fusion of many tiny seqs into weird shapes. maybe lower token_budget for small-seq queue to avoid mixing.

lucas: agreed. lowering token_budget to 96 for short-req queue in next deploy.

maya: added action items:
- revert fusion for seq<=32 (lucas)
- add historical p95 lookup in kernel selector (devin)
- reduce token_budget for short-req queue to 96 (lucas)
- add unit/regression test with heterogeneous micro-batches (maya)

sasha: I'll keep the canary running 30m and then widen if stable. tagging oncall.

perf-bot: canary metrics after 15m: small-req p95 on canary -28ms, backend error rates unchanged, KV lock wait -3%.

lucas: rolling the config to 50% now. `infractl rollout set continuous-batching.fusion.max_seq=31 --pool g1 --canary 50%`

devin: for the selector patch, I'll post a draft PR today with perf numbers from local microbench. want to avoid adding heavy runtime lookups in hot path — we can cache shape->preferred_kernel with TTL.

maya: FYI I captured a flamegraph snippet for the slow path and attached to the ticket: ticket #INF-4921. includes per-kernel GPU times and KV wait overlay.

sasha: thanks — keeping this thread for updates. if anyone sees a different cluster/pattern ping here. :eyes:
